sentences.text: Emily and Lila go to the big market on an early clear day.
Emily has visited the market before and likes the good place.
The market has many shops that sell fruit, food and water.
Emily likes the good sounds near the shops.
Lila says they should buy some fruit before they leave.
They walk past a shop that offer big fruit at a less price.
Emily and Lila choose a few piece of fruit and pay the person.
After they pay, Emily and Lila decide to explore the market.
Emily follow a strong music band while Lila follow a sign to a new shop.
Soon they know they are not together and feel very worried.
Emily look around but cannot see Lila among the many people.
She asks a fruit person if he has seen a girl with a red bag.
The person say no but he point to a shop where a child hold a bag.
Emily walk to the shop and see the child who has a good face.
The child offer a fruit.
The child say his name is Sam and he like to help people find their way.
Emily thank Sam and ask if he know a short way back to the main door.
Sam point to a street and say the way is easy.
If they kept a small speed they would arrive quickly.
Emily follows the street and soon sees a big clear sign that reads market door.
She feels good and thank Sam before she run toward the door.
Emily arrive at the main door and see Lila waiting near a big shop.
Lila is happy to see Emily and they hold.
A food person offer them a free piece and they thank him.
The person explain that the market was built many years ago and still bring many people.
Emily listen and learn that each shop has its own story and special product.
She promise to return next year and explore more of the market.
After the day end, Emily and Lila walk home feeling happy and bad.
They talk about the people they meet and the lessons they learn.
Emily think that being separate from a friend can be hard.
Emily has learned that being separate can be hard.
It also can be an opportunity to grow.
If they needed help, they would ask a near person.
The market teach that interest and good can lead to new friends and new experiences.
Later they decide to visit the area where people display new items.
Emily sees a shop that sells big material but she cannot pay for it.
A good woman who works there offers Emily a small piece for free.
Emily is happy.
Emily thank her and learn that many people value friend as much as money.
She also discover a small tea shop where she can rest and drink water.
The shop person say the market help people share stories and support each other.
A tour group arrive and begin a tour that explain the market history.
The guide say the market was create to bring farmer and city people near.
He mention that the market has survive many change and still remain a place of activity.
Emily listen carefully because she want to remember the detail for her school report.
She note that the market support local people and encourage people to try new food.
When the tour end, Emily feel good to share what she has learn with her class.
Back at home, Emily write down the event of the day in her book.
She describe each shop, each person, and each new taste she experience.
She also add a picture of the market door and the big sign she see.
Emily believe that the market will always be a place where interest meet good.
She hopes that more people will visit and find their own story in the market.
In the end, Emily learn that being separate can lead to new friend and personal growth.
She will return next year with Lila and maybe bring another friend.
The market will continue to welcome interested people and share many story.
If anyone visit, they should look for sign, ask for help, and enjoy the experience.
Remember that the market is a place where every step can teach something new.

sentences.text: Emily and Lila go to the market on a clear early day.

Lila is happy to see Emily and they hold each other before they buy some food later.

The market will continue to welcome interest visitors and share its many stories today.
If anyone visits, they should look for signs, ask for help, and enjoy the experience today.
Remember that the market is a place where every step can teach something new today.
So next time you walk into a market, keep your look open and your heart ready today.
When she thinks back, Emily sees how a simple help from Sam change her whole day.
She realizes that small acts of kind can have big effects on people who are far away.
If they meet again, they will remember the market and the many people who help them.
The market will stay a bright place where learn and sharing are always possible.
